title: Pawn structure
intro: Pawns cannot move back, so their shape decides the plans for the whole game. Learn the weak pawns to attack and the strong ones to push.

steps.text: Black's d5 pawn has no pawns beside it on the c- or e-file. No pawn can ever guard it, so pieces must. And the square in front of it, d4, can never be attacked by a black pawn.
The plan: first put a piece on d4 so the pawn cannot move (a blockade). A knight is the best blocker. Then aim more pieces at d5.
Put a knight on the blockade square.
steps.hint: Which square sits right in front of the isolated pawn?
steps.ifWrong: Blockade first: a knight on d4.
steps.ifRight: The knight on d4 can never be chased by a pawn, and the d5 pawn is stuck.

lessons.title: Doubled pawns
lessons.summary: Two pawns on one file are weaker than two side by side.

steps.text: After Bxc6 dxc6, Black has two pawns on the c-file. Doubled pawns cannot guard each other. In an endgame, White's four kingside pawns against three can make a passed pawn, while Black's extra queenside pawn cannot.

Black got something back: the two bishops and open lines. Doubled pawns are a weakness for the endgame, not a reason to panic now. So White plays calmly: castle, then d4, and trade pieces towards an ending.
Start with the calm move: get your king safe.
steps.hint: Your king is still in the centre.
steps.ifRight: The king is safe. Now the better pawns can count in the long run.

lessons.title: Passed pawns must be pushed
lessons.summary: No enemy pawn can stop it: push it.

steps.text: A passed pawn has no enemy pawns in front of it or on the files beside it. Only pieces can stop it, and every step makes it stronger. White's e-pawn is passed, and the black king is far away.

steps.hint: The knight cannot get back to the e-file in time.
steps.ifRight: Nothing can stop the pawn now.

steps.text: Another passed pawn, on the a-file, and the knight is far away. Run!
steps.hint: Count the moves: the knight needs too long to reach a8.
